For first time travelers to Nha Trang, choosing between Binh Ba Island tour and Binh Hung Island tour is one of the most common questions. Both islands are stunning, peaceful, and rich in natural beauty, yet each offers a very different travel experience.

In this article, Vietlook Travel provides a comprehensive comparison of Binh Ba and Binh Hung Islands to help you choose the destination that best suits your travel style when visiting Nha Trang.

Overview Of Binh Ba Island And Binh Hung Island – Two Hidden Gems Of Khanh Hoa

Both Binh Ba Island and Binh Hung Island are small islands located in Cam Ranh City, Khanh Hoa Province, Vietnam. Although they are geographically close, separated only by a narrow strait, each island has its own distinct charm.

As both islands lie within a military-controlled area, tourism development has been limited. This has helped preserve their pristine landscapes, clear waters, and authentic local life, offering visitors a more genuine and less commercialized island experience.

Binh Ba Island – The Lobster Island

Often referred to as “Lobster Island,” Binh Ba covers an area of just over three square kilometers and is nestled along the scenic coastal road of Binh Tien, near Vinh Hy Bay.

The island is famous for:

  • White sandy beaches

  • Crystal-clear turquoise water

  • A peaceful and relaxing atmosphere

  • Fresh seafood, especially lobster at reasonable prices

Binh Ba is ideal for travelers who enjoy a balance between relaxation, beach activities, and vibrant local food culture.

Binh Hung Island – A Quiet And Untouched Paradise

Smaller in size, Binh Hung Island spans approximately two square kilometers and is located near Hon Chut Lighthouse. Often described as a “raw gem,” Binh Hung remains largely untouched by mass tourism.

The island is known for:

  • Egg-shaped stone beaches

  • Small, hidden coves

  • Traditional fishing village life

  • A calm, rustic atmosphere

Binh Hung is perfect for travelers seeking tranquility, nature exploration, and a slower pace of life.

Highlights Of Binh Ba Island – Beaches, Seafood, And Local Life

Bai Nom Beach – Swimming And Seafood Paradise

Bai Nom is the most popular beach on Binh Ba Island, featuring soft sand, calm waters, and rocky formations. Visitors can relax on hammocks, swim, and enjoy freshly caught seafood such as lobster, squid, sea urchin, and snails.

In the evening, the area becomes a lively seafood hub, offering grilled lobster, steamed seafood, and other local specialties.

Sa Huynh Beach – Mysterious Ancient Rock Formations

Located in a restricted military zone, Sa Huynh Beach is accessible only by boat. The beach is famous for its colorful ancient rock formations shaped over millions of years.

Early morning or late afternoon is the best time to visit for photography, when sunlight creates dramatic reflections on the rocks.

Bai Chuong Beach – Sunrise And Marine Ecosystem

Bai Chuong is known as the best spot to watch sunrise on Binh Ba Island. The beach features rich marine life near the shore, making it ideal for shell collecting, light snorkeling, and photography.

Hon Rua – The Iconic Turtle-Shaped Rock

Hon Rua is one of the most iconic landmarks on the island. From above, the rock resembles a turtle emerging from the sea. It is a favorite spot for photography and panoramic views of Cam Ranh Bay.

Binh Ba Floating Village – Local Culture And Fresh Seafood

The floating village offers a glimpse into the daily life of lobster farmers. Visitors can choose live seafood directly from the cages and have it prepared on the spot, enjoying the freshest flavors of the sea.

Hon Co Beach – Where History Meets Nature

Hon Co Beach holds historical significance, having witnessed conflicts during past wars. Today, it combines natural beauty with historical stories, adding depth to the island experience.

What Makes A Binh Hung Island Tour Special?

Egg Stone Beach – A Geological Wonder

Egg Stone Beach features large, smooth, egg-shaped rocks formed by natural erosion. It is a popular photography spot, though not suitable for swimming.

Cay Me Beach – A Natural Swimming Pool

Accessible only by boat, Cay Me Beach is famous for its crystal-clear water and vibrant coral reefs, making it perfect for snorkeling and underwater photography.

Hon Chut Lighthouse – A Century-Old Viewpoint

Built over one hundred years ago, Hon Chut Lighthouse offers panoramic views of Binh Hung Island and Cam Ranh Bay, making it one of the most scenic viewpoints in the region.

Binh Tien Beach – Luxury Amid Nature

Now developed into a resort area, Binh Tien Beach combines modern comfort with untouched natural beauty, offering white sand, clear water, and peaceful surroundings.

Sweet Water Beach – Where Fresh And Salt Water Meet

Sweet Water Beach is unique for its freshwater pool hidden inside a rocky cave, right next to the sea. Visitors can enjoy both saltwater swimming and freshwater relaxation in one location.

Accommodation Options On Binh Ba And Binh Hung Islands

Both islands offer budget-friendly accommodations such as guesthouses, homestays, and floating houses. Prices are affordable, and staying with local families provides an authentic cultural experience.

Camping on the beach and staying on floating seafood farms are also popular options, especially on Binh Hung Island.

Must-Try Local Dishes On Both Islands

Seafood lovers will be delighted with specialties such as:

  • Grilled lobster

  • Sea urchin with scallion oil

  • Grilled grouper with chili salt

  • Snails, squid, and fresh fish

  • Seafood banh canh and fish noodle soup

Best Time To Visit

The ideal time to visit Binh Ba and Binh Hung Islands is from March to September, when the weather is sunny, the sea is calm, and outdoor activities are most enjoyable.

How To Get There

Travelers first reach Ba Ngoi Port in Cam Ranh, then take a boat or speedboat to the islands. On the islands, motorbike rental is the most convenient way to explore.

Travel Tips For A Perfect Trip

  • Book accommodation in advance during peak season

  • Bring cash, as card payments are limited

  • Respect military area regulations

  • Protect the environment and avoid littering

  • Foreign travelers need special permission to visit Binh Ba Island

Final Verdict: Binh Ba Or Binh Hung?

Both islands offer unique experiences:

  • Binh Ba Island is livelier, famous for lobster and developed services, ideal for travelers who enjoy vibrant island life.

  • Binh Hung Island is quieter and more untouched, perfect for nature lovers seeking peace and authenticity.

Your choice depends on your travel preferences. Either way, a Binh Ba – Binh Hung tour curated by Vietlook Travel promises an unforgettable island experience in Nha Trang.
